topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture by introducing the speaker, course structure, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer by examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic errors, inherited predisposition, and environmental exposures across global populations.

topics.label: Biological and chemical mechanisms of cancer initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms by which specific pathogens, chemical mutagens, and inflammatory agents initiate DNA damage and promote tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, experimental, and risk-benefit approaches used to determine the carcinogenicity of environmental agents.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing the central themes of environmental carcinogenesis, carcinogen potency, and everyday risk evaluation.
